glosses: to claim, to demand possession, control or responsibility
iets opeisen, aanspraak maken op iets

examples.text: In 1979 claimde Sony de naam 'Walkman'.
Na de verkiezingen claimden beide partijen de belangrijke ministerspost.

glosses: beweren

examples.text: De fabrikant claimt een toename van het vermogen van bijna 10 procent.
Het land claimt dat het uranium op grote schaal kan verrijken.

Er was natuurlijk ook niks aan de hand, want zij deden de trail gewoon op hun eigen manier. En wat was er nou mis met een beetje liften? Niks, maar het zat me toch dwars dat deze mensen na afloop claimden dat ze de PCT hadden gelopen, terwijl ze in werkelijkheid meer dan 20 procent hadden overgeslagen.

translations.source_sense_description: iets opeisen, aanspraak maken op iets

glosses: A demand of ownership made for something.

examples.text: a claim of ownership
a claim of victory

glosses: The thing claimed.
The right or ground of demanding.

examples.text: You don't have any claim on my time, since I'm no longer your employee.

glosses: A new statement of something one believes to be the truth, usually when the statement has yet to be verified or without valid evidence provided.

examples.text: The company's share price dropped amid claims of accounting fraud.

Bailey, in using accents, felt that he was 'directing to their proper pronuntiation' and showing 'the Orthoepia of the English Tongue' (title page, Dictionarium Britannicum, 1730 edition). The claim is ridiculous.
The thing is, we've even had formal confirmation from Government itself that the crucial research required to make such sweeping claims hasn't been done!

glosses: A demand of ownership for previously unowned land.

examples.text: Miners had to stake their claims during the gold rush.

glosses: A legal demand for compensation or damages.
To demand ownership of.

examples.text: Jeffrey Chuang, an economics student at University College London, said: "I am for independence. I do not think China has any right to claim Taiwan. We have confidence in our country and we know that China is not capable of doing anything to us."

glosses: To state a new fact, typically without providing evidence to prove it is true.
To demand ownership or right to use for land.
To demand compensation or damages through the courts.
To be entitled to anything; to deduce a right or title; to have a claim.

examples.text: We must know how the first ruler, from whom any one claims, came by his authority, upon what ground any one has empire

glosses: To cause the loss of.

examples.text: The attacks claimed the lives of five people.
A fire claimed two homes.

glosses: To win as a prize in a sport or competition.

examples.text: He claimed $100 after winning the top spot.

glosses: To proclaim.
To call or name.

examples.text: Nor all, that else through all the world is named[…] / Might like to this be clamed.
